items.title: Two consecutive powers of an element lying in a subring produce an element whose square and cube lie in the subring
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter morphisms.tex (Morphisms of Schemes)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file morphisms.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma says that if a ring extension contains an element outside the subring with two consecutive powers inside it, then it also contains an element outside the subring whose square and cube are inside (statement lines 11813-11820). The counted proof is complete and short: it writes the identity showing that every power of the element with exponent at least n squared lies in the subring, takes the largest exponent whose power is still outside, and observes that twice and three times that exponent exceed n squared, which gives the required element (proof lines 11822-11829). It is H2: the argument is an elementary numerical observation carried out in the counted span, and its value for the surrounding seminormality theory is as a reduction step.
